transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Sana (Redwood CSM), Jordan (TidalHealth CTO), Priya (ML Platform), Aaron (SRE), Leah (Finance)
---
00:00 Evelyn (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through a quick stability and cost sprint plan based on the usage spikes you saw in July. Sana and Marco are here to help with the ops and benching.
00:18 Jordan (CTO): Yeah thanks. We had two notable incidents last month where tail latency spiked around batch windows. Looking to understand if it's batch sizing, KV cache misses, or model choice. Also Leah from finance will want a clean story on committed vs incremental spend.
00:33 Marco (SE): Totally. I pulled the preliminary cost breakdown you shared, and there are a couple of hotspots: the reranker endpoints at high token lengths and a small fraction of long-chat sessions that drive most of the token bill.
00:49 Priya (ML Platform): One nuance is we run a 16k context model for a handful of clients, but most traffic is shorter. We can try quantizing those 16k paths but worried about quality regression.
01:05 Aaron (SRE): On the infra side we had two autoscale bursts where the dedicated pool saturated and fallback to hosted caused region-crossing tail effects. We want to avoid cross-region fallback.
01:22 Sana (CSM): Quick question Leah—from finance perspective, is the ask a clear steady-state unit cost or a proposal for a committed monthly?
01:30 Leah (Finance): Both. We need a committed baseline for budgeting, but we also want a mechanism to cap bursts. Ideally a 3-month pilot to validate the committed numbers.
01:45 Evelyn: That's doable. We'll draft an addendum for a stabilization pilot, 3 months, with agreed SLOs and burst policies. Marco will scope the perf bench.
02:05 Marco: For the bench, we'll want a 7-day trace from prod showing prefix lengths, token distributions, and a sample of long sessions. Can you share that?
02:16 Jordan: Yes we'll pull the forwarder logs. One thing — some names in the logs are obfuscated so might be tricky.
02:24 Marco: That's fine; we mostly need sequence length histograms and KV hit metrics. Also, curious about your caching TTLs and whether you do prefix normalization.
02:35 Priya: We do a crude prefix normalization: strip system prompts and minimize timestamps, but not aggressive enough to give consistent KV hits.
02:46 Marco: Ok, that can explain cache churn. If prefix variance is high, cache hit rates drop and cost per token rises.
03:02 Aaron: On the tail issue, we suspect garbage collection and small VM swaps in our cluster around midnight PST — it's a pattern that aligns with some of the latency spikes.
03:15 Marco: In our runtime, the primary things that show up at 95th percentile are GPU memory thrash when the KV cache size grows and when there are many concurrent long-seq streams. We can mitigate with smarter sharding or a cache tier.
03:30 Jordan: What would that mean operationally? Extra infra, or changes on our side?
03:35 Marco: A couple of options: 1) a Dedicated pool with pinning for the long-seq customers, 2) prefix normalization + small pre-batching to increase KV hits, or 3) quantized model variant for long contexts with fallback. Each has tradeoffs.
03:55 Leah: Financially, pinning a dedicated pool sounds expensive up front. How much delta are we looking at versus shared hosted?
04:05 Evelyn: We'll model per-endpoint steady-state and peak delta. For a pin of X GPUs, the fixed cost is visible but it flattens unit price for long sequences. We'll share a spreadsheet with scenario analysis.
04:22 Priya: We want to avoid model regression. Have you seen quantized variants that preserve output for our use case?
04:30 Marco: There are 4-bit/8-bit options; empirical regressions vary by model family. We can run a small eval against your golden prompts as part of the pilot.
04:45 Jordan: Also, security — we need specifics on KMS integration and audit logs for private deployment. Are those in the SOC2 pack?
04:55 Sana: Yes, SOC2 and ISO details are in the security folder we previously shared. For KMS we support customer-managed keys for private deployments and can surface audit events in the console. We'll re-send the matrix.
05:10 Aaron: For on-prem considerations: network egress and latency to our internal VPC will matter. We can't tolerate cross-region failover for HIPAA traffic.
05:22 Evelyn: Noted. For the pilot we can propose VPC-only endpoints with no cross-region fallback; that'll be part of the contract language.
05:33 Leah: One ask from procurement — a simple mapping that shows committed spend to expected monthly token capacity, and separate line items for burst fees.
05:44 Evelyn: We'll include that in the addendum.
06:00 Marco: Regarding bench plan, high-level: 1) run 95/99 tail microbench across your top 5 endpoints; 2) model variant A/B with quantized weights; 3) simulate burst patterns from your July traces. That should surface stability and quality tradeoffs.
06:20 Aaron: For the simulation, we can run a replay; I will anonymize and ship the trace. We also want to see the runtime's behavior when the KV cache rehydrates.
06:35 Marco: Good. Please include the KV eviction metrics and keys-per-session distributions.
06:44 Jordan: One more thread — we are considering moving our reranker to a shorter context model and moving context stitching to application-level. Would Redwood have latency benefits if we shift that work out of the model?
06:58 Marco: Typically yes — shorter context reduces KV overhead and runtime memory pressure. But stitching at app-level increases app latency vs in-model retrieval. It's a tradeoff. We can quantify.
07:12 Priya: For roadmap alignment, do you have any upcoming runtime features that would help us — e.g., prioritized KV tiers or predictable eviction?
07:22 Evelyn: We have a roadmap item for cache-tiering (Q4) and finer-grained autoscale policies (Q3 end). We'll share the roadmap snippet with dates.
07:35 Sana: We'll send the versioned roadmap link after the call.
07:44 Leah: From finance, if we commit to a 6-month reserved capacity instead of 3 months, is there a steeper discount?
07:54 Evelyn: Yes, reserved commits scale. We'll include a 3-month pilot pricing and a 6/12-month commitment table.
08:10 Jordan: Let's talk risks quickly — what would you see as primary blockers to hitting 95th%-tile goals?
08:18 Marco: Cache churn, insufficient pinned capacity for long sessions, and chaotic autoscale policies that cause cross-region failovers. Also, inconsistent prefix normalization on the app side.
08:30 Aaron: We also have legacy ingestion spikes from batch jobs at 2am; we could shift those to a maintenance window to reduce tail effects.
08:42 Priya: On testing, can Redwood simulate client-specific session distributions?
08:47 Marco: Yes, if you provide the traces we can replay and also add synthetic jitter.
08:54 Speaker 2 (likely Jordan): Great.
09:02 Evelyn: Ok next, let's nail down deliverables. Marco will run an initial bench with a small subset and report back, Sana will re-send security artifacts, and I'll produce the addendum.
09:15 Marco: I'll propose bench scripts and required inputs in a short doc. Aaron, expect to receive an artifact request.
09:24 Aaron: Roger. I'll prioritize the KV metrics and trace export.
09:30 Leah: And I'll review the financial scenarios once you send the spreadsheet. Please call out assumptions explicitly.
09:40 Evelyn: Will do. Any other questions?
09:44 Jordan: One ask — can we get a timeline for the bench results? We need something before the next leadership review in early September.
09:51 Marco: We'll aim for results by week of 2026-08-31. That gives us time to run 7-day replays.
10:03 Priya: If the bench shows small regressions on quantized models, can we try mixed routing (quantized for non-critical sessions)?
10:12 Marco: Yes, we can explore routing policies as part of the pilot.
10:20 Sana: I'll schedule the follow-up 60-minute bench kickoff for the week of 2026-08-24 and send calendar invites.
10:28 Evelyn: Thanks everyone. Quick recap in- meeting: share cost spreadsheet, collect traces, run bench, security follow-up, draft addendum.
10:42 Jordan: Thanks. Appreciate the partnership.
10:49 Meeting end.
